question.text: Which of the following expenses is NOT included in the Total Expense Ratio (TER) of a mutual fund scheme?

answer.text: Securities Transaction Tax (STT), where applicable on redemption/switch/sale of equity-oriented mutual fund units

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series V-A workbook (pp.145, 160, 162), TER includes investment management fees, trustee fees, audit fees, custodian fees, RTA fees, marketing/selling expenses (including brokerage and transaction costs), and other operational expenses. Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is a statutory levy that is borne by the scheme separately and is NOT part of TER. STT does not apply to purchases of equity-scheme units — it applies only on redemption/switch/sale of equity-oriented mutual fund units (p.160). The Trap: Investment management fees, custodian fees, and audit fees are all components of TER. Candidates may also be tempted to think STT applies to purchases — it does not for equity-scheme units; STT for mutual fund units is only on the sell/switch/redeem side. Note: Funds with high portfolio turnover incur more transaction costs and, on equity sales, more STT (outside TER), further reducing returns. Low-turnover funds tend to be more tax-efficient even though this advantage is not visible in headline TER comparisons.
